title: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: Some high-volume turboprop and turbojet engines are equipped with two-spool or split compressors. When these engines are operated at high altitudes, the
choices: low-pressure rotor will decrease in speed as the compressor load decreases in the lower density air.
low-pressure rotor will increase in speed as the compressor load decreases in the lower density air.
the high-pressure rotor will always overspeed as inlet-air density decreases.
throttle must be retarded to prevent overspeeding of the high-pressure rotor due to the lower density air.
questions.answerText: low-pressure rotor will increase in speed as the compressor load decreases in the lower density air.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A two-spool engine lets the low- and high-pressure compressor sections rotate at different speeds. At high altitude, lower air density reduces the compressor’s aerodynamic load; the low-pressure rotor can therefore accelerate unless the fuel control and operating limits constrain it.

**Engineering principle**
The low-pressure spool is mechanically independent of the high-pressure spool, so their speeds need not change together.

💡 **Memory hook:** Two spools can turn at two speeds.

🎯 **Board tip:** Track each compressor and turbine on its own shaft.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What term is used to describe a permanent and cumulative deformation of the turbine blades of a turbojet engine?
questions.answerText: Creep.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Creep is slow, permanent deformation that accumulates while a material is exposed to sustained stress, especially at elevated temperature. Turbine blades operate in hot gas under centrifugal stress, so creep can lengthen or distort a blade over time.

**Engineering principle**
Creep develops over time under sustained load; fatigue develops from repeated cyclic loading, while yielding is an immediate permanent deformation after exceeding the elastic limit.

💡 **Memory hook:** Hot metal + sustained stress + time = creep.

🎯 **Board tip:** Distinguish time-dependent creep from cycle-dependent fatigue.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: On a twin spool engine, where would the air go next after the combustor?
questions.answerText: HPT
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Combustor gases first expand through the high-pressure turbine, which extracts work to drive the high-pressure compressor. Downstream turbine stages then extract more energy before the gas reaches the exhaust.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: On a twin-spool engine, which is commonly rotated by the last stage turbine?
questions.answerText: LPC and the Fan
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
In a two-spool turbofan, the low-pressure turbine drives the low-pressure compressor and, when fitted, the fan through the low-pressure shaft. The high-pressure turbine drives the high-pressure compressor on a separate concentric shaft.

**Engineering principle**
The last turbine stages on the low-pressure spool drive the fan/LPC; the upstream high-pressure turbine drives the HPC.

💡 **Memory hook:** LP turbine → LP compressor/fan; HP turbine → HP compressor.

🎯 **Board tip:** Trace each turbine to its spool rather than assuming one shaft drives every compressor.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: It is the ratio of the mass of secondary air to the mass of primary air
questions.answerText: Bypass ratio
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Bypass ratio is bypass-duct mass flow divided by core mass flow. It compares the two airflow streams; it is not bypass flow divided by total flow. A high value means proportionally more air avoids the hot core.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: Which type of jet engine incorporates movable vanes that cause an intermittent entry of air inside the engine?
questions.answerText: Pulse jet
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A pulsejet produces thrust through repeated cycles of air admission, combustion, and exhaust rather than steady continuous flow through a compressor and turbine. Its operation is inherently intermittent and typically noisy and inefficient compared with modern gas turbines.

**Engineering principle**
Pulsejet combustion is intermittent; a turbojet’s gas path is continuous and turbine-driven.

💡 **Memory hook:** Pulse = repeated pressure pulses.

🎯 **Board tip:** The cycle, not the shape alone, identifies the engine type.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What distinguishes a turbojet from a turbofan in how thrust is produced?
choices: A turbojet derives most thrust from its core exhaust; a turbofan also accelerates bypass air
questions.answerText: A turbojet derives most thrust from its core exhaust; a turbofan also accelerates bypass air
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A turbojet derives most thrust from core exhaust. A turbofan also accelerates a substantial bypass stream with its fan, which improves propulsive efficiency at subsonic speeds by accelerating more air by a smaller amount.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What is the principal output of a turboshaft engine?
choices: Shaft power to drive a rotor or other load
Electrical voltage directly from the combustion chamber
Compressed air for cabin use only
questions.answerText: Shaft power to drive a rotor or other load
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A turboshaft is designed to deliver shaft power to an external load such as a helicopter transmission. It is not primarily designed to maximize residual exhaust thrust.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What is a turboprop optimized to provide?
choices: Shaft power to a propeller, with the propeller producing most thrust
Thrust only from a high-speed core jet
questions.answerText: Shaft power to a propeller, with the propeller producing most thrust
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A turboprop transfers most useful engine power through gearing to a propeller. The propeller accelerates a large mass of air moderately, which is efficient at low and medium aircraft speeds.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What is the Brayton cycle associated with?
questions.answerText: Idealized gas-turbine operation
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The Brayton cycle is the idealized gas-turbine cycle, with compression, approximately constant-pressure heat addition, and expansion. It models a turbine core rather than the Otto cycle of a spark-ignition piston engine.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What does bypass ratio compare in a turbofan?
choices: Mass flow through the bypass stream to mass flow through the core
questions.answerText: Mass flow through the bypass stream to mass flow through the core
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Turbofan bypass ratio = bypass air mass flow / core air mass flow. A ratio above one means more mass flows around the core than through it; it does not directly state engine efficiency.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: How does a ramjet obtain most of its compression?
choices: A rotating compressor driven by a turbine
questions.answerText: Forward speed and inlet diffusion
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A ramjet has no rotating compressor. Forward motion compresses incoming air as it diffuses in the inlet, so the engine needs speed to produce the pressure rise required for combustion.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: Why does a pulsejet produce intermittent thrust?
choices: Combustion and pressure changes occur in repeated pulses
Its propeller changes pitch every revolution
Its fuel pump stops after each cycle
questions.answerText: Combustion and pressure changes occur in repeated pulses
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A pulsejet repeats intake and combustion events rather than maintaining continuous combustion. Its pressure and momentum changes therefore produce intermittent thrust.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What is the role of a rocket engine propellant?
choices: Supply both fuel and oxidizer so combustion does not depend on atmospheric oxygen
Provide fuel only while using compressor air
questions.answerText: Supply both fuel and oxidizer so combustion does not depend on atmospheric oxygen
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A rocket carries both fuel and oxidizer, so combustion does not depend on oxygen in the surrounding atmosphere. This permits operation in space, unlike an air-breathing jet engine.

**Engineering principle**
Air-breathing engines ingest atmospheric oxygen; rockets carry their oxidizer as part of the propellant system.

💡 **Memory hook:** Rocket brings its oxygen.

🎯 **Board tip:** Identify whether the engine depends on ambient air.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: Why is a turbofan often more fuel efficient than a turbojet at subsonic transport speeds?
choices: It burns no fuel in the core
It accelerates a larger mass of air by a smaller velocity change
questions.answerText: It accelerates a larger mass of air by a smaller velocity change
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
At subsonic transport speeds a turbofan can accelerate a larger mass of air by a smaller velocity increment than a turbojet. That generally reduces kinetic energy lost in the wake for the same thrust.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: Which engine type is most directly suited to helicopter rotor drive?
questions.answerText: Turboshaft
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Certification questions depend on the regulatory edition and aircraft category named in the source. Category-specific limits and exit requirements are prescribed values, while a design-speed calculation must use the stated weight, wing area, lift coefficient, and the applicable equation with consistent units.

**Engineering principle**
Do not apply one category’s load limits or one regulation edition to another. Historical Part 23 question keys may not represent current rule wording.

💡 **Memory hook:** First identify category and rule edition.

🎯 **Board tip:** If the supplied values do not reproduce the keyed result, flag the item rather than silently forcing the arithmetic.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What is specific thrust commonly defined as?
choices: Net thrust divided by inlet airflow mass flow rate
questions.answerText: Net thrust divided by inlet airflow mass flow rate
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Specific thrust is net thrust divided by inlet air mass-flow rate. It describes thrust per unit airflow and has units of velocity; it is different from fuel consumption per unit thrust.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What causes net thrust in a jet engine?
choices: Change in momentum of the engine airflow plus pressure thrust where applicable
questions.answerText: Change in momentum of the engine airflow plus pressure thrust where applicable
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Thermodynamic questions depend on the system boundary, process constraint, and sign convention. Apply conservation of energy and the ideal-gas/process relation that matches the stated condition; use absolute temperature and absolute pressure in gas-law ratios.

**Engineering principle**
Adiabatic means no heat transfer; isentropic additionally requires reversibility. Specific heat at constant pressure differs from constant volume, and work done by a system has the opposite sign from work done on it.

💡 **Memory hook:** Name the process before choosing the equation.

🎯 **Board tip:** Check absolute versus gauge pressure and state the work sign convention.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What is the basic purpose of a gas turbine engine’s compressor?
choices: Extract all energy from the exhaust
questions.answerText: Increase air pressure before combustion
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The compressor raises incoming-air pressure before combustion. The increased pressure supports heat addition and turbine work extraction, while the compressor itself consumes shaft work from the turbine.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What is a free turbine in a turboshaft installation?
choices: A turbine stage mechanically separate from the gas-generator spool that drives the output shaft
questions.answerText: A turbine stage mechanically separate from the gas-generator spool that drives the output shaft
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A free turbine is mechanically separate from the gas-generator spool. It extracts energy from the gas-generator exhaust to drive the output shaft, letting load speed vary independently.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What does a high bypass ratio generally indicate?
choices: The engine burns only bypass air
A large mass flow bypasses the engine core relative to core flow
questions.answerText: A large mass flow bypasses the engine core relative to core flow
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A high bypass ratio means bypass-stream mass flow is large relative to core flow. This supports efficient subsonic propulsion, subject to fan size, weight, and installation tradeoffs.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: Why is a turboprop efficient at lower aircraft speeds?
choices: The propeller accelerates a large air mass by a moderate velocity change
The core exhaust alone provides all thrust
It does not require a turbine
questions.answerText: The propeller accelerates a large air mass by a moderate velocity change
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A propeller efficiently accelerates a large mass of air by a moderate velocity change at lower flight speeds. In a turboprop, the turbine provides shaft power and the propeller produces most thrust.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What is the main function of a gas-generator spool?
choices: Compress air, burn fuel, and extract enough turbine work to drive the compressor
questions.answerText: Compress air, burn fuel, and extract enough turbine work to drive the compressor
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The gas-generator spool compresses inlet air, supports combustion, and extracts turbine work to drive its compressor. A separate free power turbine can then deliver useful output shaft power.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: Why is a ramjet ineffective at standstill?
choices: It requires a propeller to rotate
It requires forward velocity to create inlet compression
questions.answerText: It requires forward velocity to create inlet compression
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A ramjet depends on forward velocity to create inlet compression. At standstill it has neither ram compression nor a compressor rotor, so it cannot establish the normal operating pressure rise.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: What is the ideal Otto-cycle efficiency trend as compression ratio increases?
choices: It is independent of compression ratio
It increases for a fixed specific-heat ratio
questions.answerText: It increases for a fixed specific-heat ratio
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Reciprocating-engine parts and cycle events are best understood by following piston motion and load transfer: the crankshaft converts piston force to torque, connecting rods transmit load, and the valve train times gas exchange. Bore and stroke set swept volume; compression ratio compares total cylinder volume at BDC with clearance volume at TDC.

**Engineering principle**
Swept displacement excludes clearance volume; compression ratio includes it. A full-floating pin moves relative to both the piston bosses and connecting-rod small end.

💡 **Memory hook:** Bore × stroke sets displacement; TDC/BDC set the volume ratio.

🎯 **Board tip:** For cycle questions, track the four strokes in order and identify when combustion pressure does useful work.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: A turbofan passes 90 kg/s through the bypass duct and 30 kg/s through the core. Find bypass ratio.
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Bypass ratio = bypass mass flow/core mass flow = (90 kg/s)/(30 kg/s) = 3. The units cancel, so bypass ratio is dimensionless.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: An engine takes in air at 250 m/s and exhausts it at 600 m/s; neglect pressure thrust and fuel mass. For 20 kg/s airflow, find thrust.
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Neglecting pressure thrust and fuel mass, F = mass flow x (V_exit - V_inlet). F = 20 kg/s x (600-250) m/s = 20 x 350 = 7,000 kg m/s^2 = 7,000 N.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: A gas turbine inlet total pressure is 100 kPa and compressor exit total pressure is 1,200 kPa. Find compressor pressure ratio.
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Compressor pressure ratio = compressor-exit total pressure/inlet total pressure = 1,200 kPa/100 kPa = 12. The pressure units cancel.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: A turbofan bypass flow is 120 kg/s and core flow is 40 kg/s. What is bypass ratio?
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Bypass ratio = 120 kg/s bypass flow / 40 kg/s core flow = 3. This ratio is dimensionless.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: A jet engine accelerates 15 kg/s of air from 200 m/s to 500 m/s. Neglect pressure thrust. Find net thrust.
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Net thrust = mass flow x velocity change = 15 kg/s x (500-200) m/s = 15 x 300 = 4,500 N, neglecting pressure thrust as instructed.
tags: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types
